title: Vice President addresses Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR in New Delhi

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR:

I. The event was inaugurated by the President of India.
II. The celebration took place at the Thyagaraj Stadium in New Delhi.
III. The occasion marked 25 years of the organization's vision and impact.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: II and III only
answerOptions.rationale: The event was inaugurated by Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, not the President, while the location and the 25-year milestone are accurate.

answerOptions.text: I and II only
answerOptions.rationale: The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, was the chief guest and inaugural speaker, making statement I incorrect.

answerOptions.text: I and III only
answerOptions.rationale: While the Silver Jubilee signifies 25 years, the inauguration was performed by the Vice President, not the President.

answerOptions.text: I, II, and III
answerOptions.rationale: This option is incorrect because statement I wrongly attributes the inauguration to the President instead of the Vice President.

questions.hint: Identify the specific high-ranking official mentioned as the chief guest in the text.

questions.question: In his address, Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasized the national vision of 'Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi'. What is the primary objective of this approach according to the discourse?

answerOptions.text: Balancing civilisational pride with modern aspirations and development
answerOptions.rationale: The text states this approach connects children to their roots (Virasat) while equipping them for a changing future (Vikas).

answerOptions.text: Prioritizing industrial growth over the preservation of cultural heritage
answerOptions.rationale: The slogan suggests a dual focus rather than prioritizing one over the other, specifically seeking to maintain cultural roots.

answerOptions.text: Replacing traditional education with purely technical and modern vocational skills
answerOptions.rationale: The speech advocates for nurturing value-driven citizens rooted in culture, not replacing traditions with technical skills.

answerOptions.text: A government scheme aimed exclusively at urban infrastructure in Delhi-NCR
answerOptions.rationale: While the event was in Delhi, 'Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi' is described as a broader national vision for the youth's character and the nation's progress.

questions.hint: Think about the literal translation of the Hindi terms in the context of growth and heritage.

questions.question: What does the concept of 'Krishnarpanam', as described during the Rajatha Jayanti celebrations, signify?

answerOptions.text: The dedication of one’s thoughts, actions, and talents to a higher purpose
answerOptions.rationale: The Vice President explained that this concept embodies the essence of selfless action and dharma as taught by Lord Krishna.

answerOptions.text: A financial grant provided by the Ministry of Minority Affairs to cultural groups
answerOptions.rationale: The text describes it as a 'sacred offering' and a spiritual/philosophical concept, not a financial grant.

answerOptions.text: A specific curriculum designed for primary schools in New Delhi
answerOptions.rationale: Krishnarpanam is referred to as a sacred offering and a philosophical embodiment of teachings rather than a formal school curriculum.

answerOptions.text: The inauguration of a new stadium named after Lord Krishna
answerOptions.rationale: The event was held at the Thyagaraj Stadium; Krishnarpanam is the name of the offering/celebration theme.

questions.hint: Consider the philosophical meaning of making an offering of one's self and deeds.

title: Prime Minister shares glimpses of his address to the Nation

questions.question:
Regarding the Prime Minister's address on the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, consider the following statements:
I. The opposition's resistance is described as an insult to the sentiments of the Constitution makers.
II. The Prime Minister characterized the amendment as a 'Mahayagya' intended to give 'new flight' to Indian women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: I only
answerOptions.rationale: While statement I is mentioned in the text, it is not the only correct statement, as the Prime Minister also explicitly used the term 'Mahayagya' for the amendment.

answerOptions.text: II only
answerOptions.rationale: While statement II accurately reflects the PM's metaphor for the amendment, statement I is also a primary claim made in the source material regarding the Constitution makers.

answerOptions.text: Both I and II
answerOptions.rationale: The source material confirms that the PM viewed the opposition as insulting the Constitution makers' sentiments and described the amendment as a 'Mahayagya' for women's empowerment.

answerOptions.text: Neither I nor II
answerOptions.rationale: Both statements are direct reflections of the Prime Minister's assertions regarding the legislative intent and the nature of the opposition's actions.

questions.hint: Consider the specific metaphors and historical references the Prime Minister used to justify the importance of the Act.

questions.question: Which of the following political parties were specifically cited by the Prime Minister as having 'committed foeticide' (bhroon-hatya) of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment?

answerOptions.text: Congress, TMC, Samajwadi Party, and DMK
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister explicitly listed these four parties as the ones responsible for the metaphorical 'foeticide' of the amendment.

answerOptions.text: Congress, CPI(M), RJD, and AAP
answerOptions.rationale: While these are opposition entities, they were not the specific group of four parties listed in the PM's address provided in the text.

answerOptions.text: TMC, DMK, BRS, and Shiv Sena (UBT)
answerOptions.rationale: Only TMC and DMK from this list were specifically mentioned in the Prime Minister's series of posts regarding the amendment's rejection.

answerOptions.text: Samajwadi Party, BSP, JDS, and Congress
answerOptions.rationale: Though the Samajwadi Party and Congress are mentioned, the text does not include BSP or JDS in the specific list of parties accused of 'foeticide'.

questions.hint: Look for the specific list of regional and national parties mentioned in the second post.

questions.question: What primary psychological or political factor does the Prime Minister attribute to the 'Parivarvadi' (dynastic) parties' opposition to women's reservation?

answerOptions.text: A disagreement over the technical implementation of the quota
answerOptions.rationale: The text suggests the opposition is rooted in a fear of losing power rather than technical or administrative disagreements.

answerOptions.text: Fear that empowered women will threaten their existing leadership
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister explicitly states that dynastic parties fear that if women become empowered, their own leadership will be in danger.

answerOptions.text: Concerns regarding the constitutional validity of the amendment
answerOptions.rationale: The PM dismisses the opposition's motives as self-serving fear rather than legitimate legal or constitutional concerns.

answerOptions.text: A belief that the reservation percentage was insufficient
answerOptions.rationale: There is no mention in the text of the opposition wanting a higher percentage; instead, their motive is framed as a protection of dynastic interests.

questions.hint: Focus on the PM's critique of family-run political structures and their survival instincts.

questions.question: The Prime Minister expressed a personal hope that the Congress party would use the Women's Reservation Bill as an opportunity to do which of the following?

answerOptions.text: Propose a more comprehensive bill
answerOptions.rationale: The PM's focus was not on legislative improvements from the opposition but on a moral or historical correction.

answerOptions.text: Collaborate with regional parties for a consensus
answerOptions.rationale: The text emphasizes the Congress party's individual missed opportunity for internal atonement rather than coalition building.

answerOptions.text: Atone for their past 'sins' (paapon ka prayaschit)
answerOptions.rationale: The PM specifically mentions he hoped the Congress would use this opportunity for 'prayaschit' (atonement/penance) for past mistakes regarding women's reservation.

answerOptions.text: Demonstrate their commitment to secularism
answerOptions.rationale: The address specifically focuses on gender representation and 'Nari Shakti' rather than the principle of secularism.

questions.hint: Think of the religious or moral term used to describe making up for past errors.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister's address, what is the predicted consequence for those who 'strike at the self-respect and self-esteem' of the nation's women?

answerOptions.text: They will face legal challenges in the Supreme Court
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister's warning is framed as a political and social reckoning from the people, not a specific legal process.

answerOptions.text: They will not be able to escape the wrath (akrosh) of mothers, sisters, and daughters
answerOptions.rationale: The text states that those hurting 'Nari Shakti' will not be able to avoid the anger or indignation of the women of the country.

answerOptions.text: They will be barred from participating in future 'Mahayagyas'
answerOptions.rationale: While 'Mahayagya' is a metaphor for the bill, the consequence for opposition is described in terms of the public outrage of women.

answerOptions.text: They will be forced to apologize to the Constitution makers
answerOptions.rationale: While their actions are called an insult to the founders, the consequence is specifically tied to the 'akrosh' (outrage) of the women themselves.

questions.hint: The PM uses a word describing a strong emotional response from the female population.

questions.question: In the context of the PM's statements, what does the term 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' represent?

answerOptions.text: A new welfare scheme for maternal health
answerOptions.rationale: The context of the discussion is clearly centered on 'Mahila Arakshan' or Women's Reservation, not a health scheme.

answerOptions.text: A constitutional amendment regarding women's reservation
answerOptions.rationale: The text refers to it as an amendment related to women's reservation ('Mahila Arakshan') and a 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam'.

answerOptions.text: A judicial guideline for protecting women's dignity
answerOptions.rationale: The PM refers to it as an 'Adhiniyam' (Act/Bill) and an amendment, which implies a legislative rather than a judicial origin.

answerOptions.text: A policy for increasing women's participation in the labor force
answerOptions.rationale: The PM specifically focuses on the political empowerment and reservation aspect rather than economic labor policies.

questions.hint: Look for the Hindi term used alongside 'Arakshan' in the text.

questions.question: How does the Prime Minister describe the impact of the opposition's stance on the legacy of the Indian Constitution's architects?

answerOptions.text: As a fulfillment of the vision of the preamble
answerOptions.rationale: The PM argues the opposite, stating that the opposition's actions are a betrayal of the founders' vision.

answerOptions.text: As a necessary check and balance on executive power
answerOptions.rationale: The PM characterizes the opposition's role not as a democratic check, but as a derogatory act against the nation's founders.

answerOptions.text: As an insult to the sentiments of the Constitution makers
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that by opposing the reservation, the parties have 'insulted the feelings of the makers of the Constitution'.

answerOptions.text: As a move toward a more federal structure
answerOptions.rationale: The critique is focused on the betrayal of constitutional values regarding gender empowerment, not federalism.

questions.hint: The PM links the current legislative debate back to the original authors of India's foundational document.

questions.question: Which specific metaphor is used in the text to describe the act of blocking or opposing the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment?

answerOptions.text: A hurdle in the path of progress
answerOptions.rationale: While logically true in the PM's view, the specific and more severe metaphor used is 'bhroon-hatya'.

answerOptions.text: Foeticide (Bhroon-hatya)
answerOptions.rationale: The PM used this specific, evocative term to describe how the Congress and other parties killed the amendment in its early stages.

answerOptions.text: A dark cloud over democracy
answerOptions.rationale: The PM's language is more specifically targeted at the 'life' of the amendment itself using biological metaphors.

answerOptions.text: An eclipse of the nation's pride
answerOptions.rationale: This is a plausible distractor, but the text specifically uses 'bhroon-hatya' to describe the opposition's impact on the amendment.

questions.hint: The PM uses a term typically associated with the termination of a life before birth.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister, the 'new flight' (nai udaan) for the women of Bharatvarsh was intended to be facilitated through which mechanism?

answerOptions.text: Economic subsidies for women entrepreneurs
answerOptions.rationale: The 'flight' mentioned is specifically linked to the 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' amendment, which concerns political reservation.

answerOptions.text: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment
answerOptions.rationale: The PM states that the amendment was a 'Mahayagya' meant to give a 'new flight' to the women of India.

answerOptions.text: Educational quotas in premier institutions
answerOptions.rationale: The text focuses on the specific legislative amendment for reservation, not general educational quotas.

answerOptions.text: The dissolution of dynastic political parties
answerOptions.rationale: While the PM criticizes these parties, the 'flight' itself is provided by the Act/Amendment, not the removal of the parties.

questions.hint: Identify the legislative instrument the Prime Minister is defending in his posts.

questions.question: The PM's address suggests that opposition to women's reservation is not merely a political difference but a strike against which of the following?

answerOptions.text: International diplomatic standing
answerOptions.rationale: The address is focused on the internal socio-political fabric and the self-respect of Indian women, not foreign relations.

answerOptions.text: The economic stability of the middle class
answerOptions.rationale: The PM focuses on the dignity and power of 'Nari Shakti' (women power) rather than economic indicators.

answerOptions.text: The self-respect and self-esteem of women power (Nari Shakti)
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that those who strike at the 'svabhiman' (self-respect) and 'atmasamman' (self-esteem) of women will face their wrath.

answerOptions.text: The legislative authority of the Parliament
answerOptions.rationale: The emphasis is on the personal and collective dignity of women as a social force rather than just a procedural insult to Parliament.

questions.hint: Look for the Hindi terms 'svabhiman' and 'atmasamman' and what they refer to in the text.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the nation
